title: Finite-Tor direct image and scalar projection over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $R=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $t$, and put $A=R/t^nR$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ be a $k$-morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Work in ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning that tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. There is $c_h\geq0$ such that $R^qh_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q>c_h$. If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, $a\leq b$, then $Rh_*K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+c_h]$. For every unital finite commutative $A$-algebra $B$, scalar extension $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ takes $D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(W,B)$ for $W=U,V$, preserving the Tor interval. The canonical $B$-linear comparison $T_VRh_{*,A}K\to Rh_{*,B}T_UK$, defined as the transpose of the scalar-extended inverse-image/direct-image counit, is an isomorphism. Upon exact restriction of scalars it is the finite-constant projection map followed by the canonical direct-image restriction comparison [def-kun-projection-formula-map, lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. No flatness of $B/A$ or absolute cohomological-dimension bound for $k$ is assumed.

source.place: Locality and Charts, direct-image coefficient input; extraction of old item Steps 2–3, following Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.17

proof.text: The valuation-ring theorem [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and finite-quotient theorem [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] make $A$ a finite local ring with residue field $\kappa=A/(t)$. Every ideal of a finite ring is generated by its finite set of elements, so $A$ is Noetherian. Every finite $A$-module is finitely presented: its elements give a finite free surjection and its kernel is a finite set, hence finitely generated. This applies to $\kappa$ and to the underlying $A$-module of any finite $A$-algebra $B$. Since the valuation extends the $\ell$-adic valuation, $|\ell|_E<1$, so $\ell\in(t)$ and $\ell^n\in(t^n)$. Thus $\ell^nA=0$, and also $\ell^nB=0$. The integer $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$.

source.place: Section 6.7 coefficient hypotheses, before Theorem 6.7.1; elementary coefficient arithmetic from the cited DVR statements

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f10], clause (1), to the given morphism $h$ of finite-type $k$-schemes. By [def-kun-cd] this supplies a nonnegative integer $c_h$ annihilating all higher direct images of torsion abelian sheaves above $c_h$. An $A$-module sheaf is killed by $\ell^n$, hence is such a torsion sheaf. Apply [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] to $\mathbf Z\to A$ and to this sheaf in degree zero. It identifies the underlying abelian higher direct image of the module-sheaf direct image with the abelian-sheaf higher direct image. Exact scalar restriction detects a zero module sheaf, because it retains its underlying abelian sheaf [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Therefore $R^qh_{*,A}M=0$ for $q>c_h$, for every $M$. Only the relative clause (1) of 0F10 is used; no assertion about $\operatorname{cd}(k)$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd (1); Tag 0F0Z, definition-cd-f; module comparison: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD

proof.text: Put $F=Rh_{*,A}K$. The coefficient ring is finite and killed by the integer $\ell^n$ invertible in $k$, and $U,V$ are finite type over this field. The input $K$ is bounded constructible. Thus [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] gives $F\in D^b_c(V,A)$. Its statement explicitly allows nonseparated $h$ and an arbitrary field.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1 and Lemma 6.7.2, finite-coefficient constructibility input; arbitrary-field ordinary-etale version in the cited existing node

proof.text: Let $L=K\otimes_A^L\kappa_U$. The Tor hypothesis [def-kun-tor-amplitude] gives $\mathcal H^q(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The source and target module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and $h_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to a bounded-below representative of $L$. Its page is $E_2^{r,q}=R^rh_*\mathcal H^q(L)$, with $r\geq0$; Step 2 makes it zero for $r>c_h$, and the Tor hypothesis makes it zero for $q\notin[a,b]$. Thus the page is supported in $[0,c_h]\times[a,b]$. All later pages have the same support, so in total degree outside $[a,b+c_h]$ every graded quotient of the finite abutment filtration supplied by that theorem is zero. Successively using $F^r/F^{r+1}=0$ and the zero final term of that finite filtration gives $\mathcal H^i(Rh_*L)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b+c_h]$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17, residue-tensor argument made explicit using the finite rectangle of the existing truncation spectral sequence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] with $M=\kappa$, $N=c_h$ and the bounded-above complex $K$. Step 1 checks Noetherianity and finite presentation, and Step 2 checks the uniform vanishing hypothesis for all module sheaves. It identifies $F\otimes_A^L\kappa_V$ with $Rh_*(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_U)=Rh_*L$ by the canonical projection map. Step 4 therefore gives residue-tensor vanishing outside $[a,b+c_h]$. Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] to the bounded constructible object $F$ of Step 3, with exactly the coefficient ring $\mathcal O_E/t^n$ and its residue field. It gives Tor amplitude $[a,b+c_h]$ for $F$, proving its membership in $D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17, finite-constant projection; residue test expanded in the cited DAG node

proof.text: For either $W=U$ or $V$, and $J\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$ with Tor interval $[r,s]$, form the actual $B$-linear derived extension $J_B=T_WJ$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. A K-flat representative $P$ gives $P\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ with the $B_W$-action through the second factor. Its underlying $A$-complex is precisely $J\otimes_A^LB_W$, by the K-flat definition [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Hence its underlying cohomology vanishes outside $[r,s]$, by [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Restriction changes no cohomology groups [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so $J_B$ is already bounded as a $B$-complex. This observation does not assert constructibility yet.

source.place: Paragraphs (1) and (2), derived extension and cohomological boundedness on its finite-Tor domain

proof.text:
We now establish constructibility and the full $B$-Tor interval of $J_B$. Finite-type schemes over a field are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and in particular qcqs, so [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] applies to $W$ and the finite Noetherian rings $A,B$. It takes $J$ to a pro-etale constructible complex of Tor amplitude $[r,s]$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], clause (2), its pro-etale scalar extension is constructible of $B$-Tor amplitude $[r,s]$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], for $A_W	o B_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the K-flat extension $J\mapsto J_B$ and the pro-etale $(-)_B$ (K-flat, clause (1)) are left adjoint to derived restriction of scalars. The global functors $T,S$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-scalar-extension-local-systems] are left adjoints of the same functors, so uniqueness of adjoints gives $T\cong(-)_B$ and $S\cong(-)_B$, and its comparison $S
u_W^*\cong
u_W^*T$ identifies $(
u_W^*J)_B$ with $
u_W^*J_B$. Essential surjectivity of the $B$-coefficient equivalence in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies $J'\in D^b_{ctf}(W_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $
u_W^*J'\simeq
u_W^*J_B$. Both $J'$ and $J_B$ are bounded below (Step 6). Full faithfulness of $
u_W^*$ on $D^+$ in [sk-prop-sf-comparison] lifts this isomorphism and its inverse, giving $J'\simeq J_B$. Consequently $J_B$ is bounded constructible. The interval equivalence in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] now gives its $B$-Tor interval $[r,s]$ from that of $
u_W^*J_B$. This works for every finite $A$-algebra $B$, without flatness, and for both schemes $W$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), scalar preservation, transferred to the ordinary etale site by the existing coefficient and finite-Tor comparison theorems

proof.text: Let $\beta_K:T_VF\to Rh_{*,B}T_UK$ be the specified counit transpose. Steps 5--7 imply $T_UK$ and $T_VF$ are bounded, so the domain requirements of [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection] hold. Its statement identifies the restricted map, followed by $d: \operatorname{Res}Rh_{*,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}$, with $\mathrm{PF}_h(K,B_V[0])$. The isomorphism $d$ is exactly [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] with the finitely presented underlying $A$-module $B$ from Step 1, the bounded-above $K$, and the bound $c_h$ from Step 2. It says that this projection morphism is invertible. Thus $d\circ\operatorname{Res}(\beta_K)$ is invertible, and so is $\operatorname{Res}(\beta_K)$. Exact restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms: its cone has the same underlying cohomology sheaves before and after restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Hence $\beta_K$ is a $B$-linear isomorphism. This also proves the claimed normalization of the map, rather than merely the existence of an unspecified isomorphism.

The split creates no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are byte-identical to the unsplit base, so the target is not weakened. There is no re-split note, the item is not on the dropped list, and the closure has no cycle. Stacks 0F10(1)/0F0Z: cd(f)<inf holds over any field without separatedness, which is exactly how Step 2 uses lem-kun-0f10 (1). Step 2 extends the bound to all A-module sheaves through the restriction comparison for Z->A. Step 3 meets every hypothesis of thm-dg (finite A killed by ell^n, which is invertible in k; nonseparated allowed). In Step 4 the E2 spectral sequence on a bounded L has its page in [0,c_h]x[a,b], and its finite filtration gives the bound. In Step 5 the projection formula with M=kappa and N=c_h, then the residue test for O_E/varpi^n, give Tor amplitude [a,b+c_h]. Step 6 gets boundedness of J_B from Tor amplitude tested against B_W. Step 8 uses the scalar-mate node (the same beta), the projection formula for M=B (finitely presented) and the fact that Res reflects isomorphisms. This also proves the stated normalization. One fault (C3/C4), repaired: Step 7 identified nu^*J_B with (nu^*J)_B through lem-weil-pbc-derived-scalar-extension-local-systems, but that node only asserts the existence of some left adjoints T,S of derived restriction together with a comparison S nu^* = nu^* T. I added lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction (K-flat L phi^* is left adjoint to Res on any site) and uniqueness of adjoints, so T and S are the actual extensions. uses, proof_deps and tool_uses are updated in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-pur-etale-finite-tor-direct-image-coefficients.json. Advisory: the D_ctf of det-pe and the D_ctf of det-sp are written with different constructibility definitions, but for discrete finite rings they coincide. Edge cases checked: K=0, h=id, n=1, nonflat B=kappa and kappa[eps], B=0, infinite cd(k), nonseparated h.
